title: Perseus: A Bioinformatics Platform for Integrative Analysis of Proteomics Data
author: Juergen Cox
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnk7mczn
materials: Get familiar with the Software and its five main sections: Load, Processing, Analysis, Multi-processing, and Export ( see Fig.2). Fig. 2 Interfaces of Perseus and the augmented data matrix format. ( a ) Perseus extends over five interfaces, each of which includes various analysis and transformation functionalities and visualization possibilities. ( b ) Experimental design is specified as annotation (e.g., treatment vs. control groups) or numerical rows (e.g., variable concentration). Multiple annotation rows can be specified that allow biological and technical replicates to be analyzed together. ( c ) The data is organized in a matrix format where typically all samples are displayed as columns and all proteins as rows. ( d ) Additional protein information can be added in the form of Numerical, Categorical, or Text annotations In the workflow panel, change the name of the data matrix from matrix 1 to InitialData by right-clicking the node and changing the Alternative name box. Close the pop-up window. Explore the right-most panel of Perseus, which contains useful information such as number of main columns and number of rows.
Switch the view to the “Data” tab.
Download the file to the Perseus/conf/annotations folder.

steps.title: Load Data into Perseus
steps.instruction: Import the proteomics data matrix into the software.

substeps.instruction: Go to the 'Load' section and click 'Generic matrix upload'.
Navigate to the tab-delimited txt file (must contain a header row).
Ensure 'Regional and Language Options' are set to English to avoid decimal separator errors.
Transfer expression columns to the 'Main columns' window.
Transfer additional numerical data to the 'Numerical columns' window.
Ensure identifier columns (e.g., protein IDs) are selected as 'Text columns'.
Click OK.

steps.title: Filter and Transform Data
steps.instruction: Clean the dataset by removing contaminants and transforming the scale.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Processing ➔ Filter rows ➔ Filter rows based on categorical column' to exclude proteins identified by site, reverse database matches, or contaminants.
Apply additional filters for quantitative measures, such as minimum number of quantified peptides or maximum q-value, if needed.
Transform data to a logarithmic scale via 'Processing ➔ Basic ➔ Transform' (e.g., log2(x)).

steps.title: Generate Summary Statistics
steps.instruction: Calculate basic statistics for the expression columns.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Processing ➔ Basic ➔ Summary statistics (columns)'.
Transfer all expression columns to the right-hand side and click OK.

steps.title: Filter Based on Valid Values
steps.instruction: Remove protein groups with excessive missing values.

substeps.instruction: Select the InitialData matrix in the workflow window.
Go to 'Processing ➔ Filter rows ➔ Filter rows based on valid values'.
Set 'Min. valids' parameter to 'Percentage' and use the default value of 70% for 'Min. percentage of values'.
Click OK.

steps.title: Perform Exploratory Data Visualization
steps.instruction: Visually inspect data distributions and sample correlations.

substeps.instruction: Create histograms: Go to 'Analysis ➔ Visualization ➔ Histograms', select samples of interest, and click OK. Use 'Properties', 'Fit width', and 'Fit height' to adjust. Export as pdf, tiff, or png.
Create multi-scatter plots: Go to 'Analysis ➔ Visualization ➔ Multi scatter plot', select samples, and click OK. Adjust using 'Fit width' and 'Fit height'.

Analyze correlations: In the scatter plot window, select 'Pearson correlation' from the 'Display in plots' drop-down menu. Click a plot to enlarge it and use the 'Point' table to examine specific proteins across pairwise comparisons.
Calculate column correlation: Go to 'Processing ➔ Basic ➔ Column correlation' and ensure Type is set to 'Pearson correlation'.
Visualize sample correlations: Go to 'Analysis ➔ Clustering/PCA ➔ Hierarchical clustering' and set a continuous color gradient.

steps.title: Perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
steps.instruction: Analyze sample separation and identify driving proteins.

substeps.instruction: Navigate back to the data matrix in the workflow panel.
Remove all proteins with missing values by repeating the 'Filter rows based on valid values' step with the percentage parameter set to 100%.
Go to 'Analysis ➔ Clustering/PCA ➔ Principal component analysis' and click OK.
Color-code samples by experimental condition using the 'Symbol color' button in the right-hand table.
Substitute Component 1 and 2 with other components from the drop-down menu to find optimal sample separation.
Identify driving proteins: In the loadings plot, set selection Mode to 'rectangular selection', draw a rectangle around dots in the upper right corner to highlight proteins in the table.

steps.title: Normalize Data
steps.instruction: Correct for systematic shifts or skewness.

substeps.instruction: Navigate back to the data matrix used before the 100% valid value filter.
Go to 'Processing ➔ Normalization ➔ Z-score'.
Set 'Matrix access' to 'Columns' and select the 'Use median' option.

steps.title: Annotate Samples and Proteins
steps.instruction: Assign experimental conditions and add biological annotations.

substeps.instruction: Define experimental conditions: Go to 'Processing ➔ Annot. rows ➔ Categorical annotation rows'. Use 'Create' to manually specify conditions or 'Create from experiment name' using regular expressions.
Download annotations: Select 'Annotation download' from the top left drop-down menu and click the link in the pop-up window to select a file (e.g., 'mainAnnot.homo_sapiens.txt.gz' for humans).

Add annotations: Go to 'Processing ➔ Annot. columns ➔ Add annotation', select the downloaded file as Source, and set the 'UniProt column' parameter to the column containing UniProt identifiers (e.g., Protein IDs).
Transfer desired annotation categories to the right-hand side and click OK.

steps.title: Perform Differential Expression Analysis
steps.instruction: Identify proteins that are significantly different between conditions.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Processing ➔ Tests' and select the appropriate test (e.g., 'Multiple-sample tests' for >2 conditions, 'One-sample tests' for one condition with replicates, or 'Two-sample tests' for two conditions).
Set the 'Grouping' parameter to the categorical row containing experimental conditions.
Set 'S0' parameter to 0 for standard t-test or modify as per Tusher et al.
Set 'Use for truncation' for multiple hypothesis testing correction (Permutation-based FDR with at least 250 repetitions is recommended; Benjamini-Hochberg is a more conservative alternative).
Specify an optional suffix for output columns.
Filter for significance: Go to 'Processing ➔ Filter rows ➔ Filter rows based on categorical column', set Column to 'ANOVA Significant' and Mode to 'Keep matching rows'.
Perform post-hoc analysis: Go to 'Processing ➔ Tests ➔ Post-hoc tests', set the same 'Grouping' as the ANOVA test, set the FDR threshold, and compute Tukey’s honestly significant difference (THSD).

steps.title: Cluster and Visualize Differentially Expressed Proteins
steps.instruction: Group significant proteins and visualize their expression profiles.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Analysis ➔ Clustering/PCA ➔ Hierarchical clustering' and click OK.
Adjust the color scale (red for high, green for low) using the 'Change color gradient' button.
Define protein clusters by clicking node junctions in the protein tree or using the 'Define row clusters' button to specify a number of clusters.
Inspect profile plots for selected clusters, modify the 'Color scale', and export images via 'Export image'.
Click 'Export row clustering' in the ribbon menu to add cluster information to a new data matrix.

steps.title: Perform Functional Enrichment Analysis
steps.instruction: Identify biological processes enriched in the identified protein clusters.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Multi-proc. ➔ Matching rows by name'.
Set the 'Base matrix' to the data matrix generated before filtering for ANOVA significant hits.
Set the 'Other matrix' to the last generated matrix.
Set the 'Matching column' for both matrices to a common identifier (e.g., Protein IDs).
Transfer the 'Cluster' category to the right-hand side in the categorical columns section and click OK.
Go to 'Processing ➔ Annot. columns ➔ Fisher exact test', set the 'Column' parameter to 'Cluster', and click OK.
